:::{#def-generated-sigma-algebra}
#### $\sigma$-algebra generated by a collection

Let $\coll$ be a [collection](sets-functions.qmd#def-collection) of subsets of a set $S$.
The **$\sigma$-algebra generated by** $\coll$,
written $\gensalg{\coll}$,
is the intersection of all the $\sigma$-algebras on $S$ that contain every set in $\coll$.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#rem-generated-sigma-algebra-smallest}
#### The smallest $\sigma$-algebra containing $\coll$

$\gensalg{\coll}$ is a $\sigma$-algebra by @thm-sigma-algebra-intersection
(the collection of all subsets of $S$ is one of the $\sigma$-algebras intersected,
by @thm-power-set-sigma-algebra, so there is at least one).
It contains every set in $\coll$,
and it is contained in every other $\sigma$-algebra on $S$ that does,
so it is the smallest $\sigma$-algebra on $S$ that contains $\coll$.

:::
